lesson.text: Quick memory: on a number line from 0 to 1, 1/2 is halfway. Where is 2/4? Also halfway!
A fraction wall shows it: 1/2 covers the same space as 2/4 and as 4/8. Fractions of the same size are equivalent: 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8.
More equal fractions: 1/3 = 2/6, 2/3 = 4/6 and 3/4 = 6/8. Cut every part into 2: there are twice as many parts, and twice as many are shaded.
The same bottom number: the parts are the same size, so more parts is bigger. 5/8 > 3/8.
The same top number: the bigger the bottom number, the smaller each part. 1/3 > 1/6, and 2/3 > 2/8, because thirds are bigger than eighths.
Adding with the same bottom number: 2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5, three fifths. Add the top numbers and keep the bottom one. Taking away works the same way: 4/6 − 1/6 = 3/6.
Hoot's puzzle: Zara eats 3/8 of a pie and Bram eats 2/8. Together they eat 3/8 + 2/8 = 5/8, and 3/8 is left, because 8/8 is the whole pie. Next, in grade 4: fractions with different bottom numbers.

exercises.hint: On the wall, find where 1/2 ends. How many quarters fit up to there?
exercises.explain: 2 quarters cover the same space as 1 half: 1/2 = 2/4.

exercises.hint: Do the two shaded parts end at the same place on the wall?
exercises.explain: Yes: 2 sixths cover the same space as 1 third.

exercises.hint: The parts are the same size. Compare how many.
Add the top numbers and keep the bottom number.
Would you rather have half a cake or an eighth of it?
How many sixths make one third?
The same number of parts. Which parts are bigger: thirds or eighths?
Take away the top numbers and keep the bottom number.
exercises.explain: 5 sixths − 2 sixths = 3 sixths: 3/6, which is the same as 1/2.

exercises.prompt: Put these fractions in order, smallest first.
exercises.hint: The bigger the bottom number, the smaller the part.
Half of the parts must be shaded.
4 eighths is half of the whole.
exercises.explain: 4 is half of 8, so 4/8 is a half: 4/8 = 1/2. On the fraction wall, 4 eighths cover the same space as 1 half.

exercises.hint: Add the eighths. How many eighths make a whole?

exercises.prompt: Tilly ate 2/3 of a cake. Zara ate 2/5 of a cake of the same size. Who ate more?
exercises.hint: The same number of parts. Which parts are bigger?
exercises.explain: Thirds are bigger than fifths, so 2/3 > 2/5: Tilly ate more.

exercises.prompt: Bram paints 3/10 of a wall on Monday and 4/10 on Tuesday. What fraction of the wall is painted?
Put these fractions in order, smallest first.
exercises.hint: The top numbers are the same. The bigger the bottom number, the smaller each part.
exercises.explain: Twelfths are the smallest parts and quarters the biggest: 3/12 < 3/8 < 3/6 < 3/4.

exercises.prompt: Zara eats 2/8 of a pizza and Bram eats 1/4 of it. What fraction of the pizza is left? Answer in eighths.
exercises.hint: Change 1/4 into eighths first, so all the parts are the same size.
exercises.explain: 1/4 is the same as 2/8. Together they eat 2/8 + 2/8 = 4/8. The whole pizza is 8/8, so 8/8 − 4/8 = 4/8 is left: half the pizza.
